subject: Phase 100240: Multi-Host Sync Protocol Implementation Review
verdict_justification: The Phase 100240 implementation fails critical quality gates: make check / make lint fail due to an unused import (ErrorCode in journal_row.rs:29), and the required 90% per-file function coverage gate failed on 5 source files (postgres_sync.rs, client.rs, http.rs, protocol.rs, server.rs). Furthermore, sub-millisecond item updates crash SQLite due to duplicate audit_events.id, and triples are omitted from the client push change feed.

issues.title: Falsified Coverage Defense and Under-90% Function Coverage Across Five Source Files
issues.why_it_matters: The project enforces a strict ≥90% per-file function coverage gate. The developer claimed that low numbers were an LLVM dual-codegen artifact and that scoped runs were 90-100%, but scoped runs also fail (protocol.rs 60.00%, server.rs 64.71%, http.rs 69.57%, client.rs 79.17%, postgres_sync.rs 80.00%, sqlite_sync.rs 87.04%).
issues.impact: Multiple production functions across clio-sync and clio-store are unexercised in tests, violating core AGENTS.md rules and masking potential defects.
issues.evidence: Output of make coverage and cargo llvm-cov --package clio-sync: protocol.rs (60.00% func, 8 missed), server.rs (64.71% func, 12 missed), http.rs (69.57% func, 7 missed), client.rs (79.17% func, 5 missed), postgres_sync.rs (80.00% func, 9 missed), sqlite_sync.rs (87.04% func, 7 missed). Functions like subject_is_shredded and dead_letter_status have zero test invocations.
issues.proposed_fix: Add comprehensive unit/integration tests targeting unhit functions across clio-sync and clio-store, and prune unneeded functions to bring all reported files above 90% function coverage.
issues.resolution: Real deficit, not only an artifact. cargo-llvm-cov's per-cfg instantiation is genuine, but it masked unreached error-mapper closures. Removed the unreachable closures (content_for, crypto::seal, server::write_json, journal_row_to_mutation error arms), replaced them with shared unit-tested mapper functions, extracted push-side packaging into client_feed.rs, and added the missing tests (protocol cursor/watermark error shapes, content_value, http framing/io mappers, server error seams). Stale target/llvm-cov-target artifacts are cleared with `cargo llvm-cov clean --workspace` before the gate.
issues.resolution_evidence: make coverage exit 0; aggregate functions 98.86% (2899, 33 missed), lines 97.87%. No reported file below 90% on functions or lines. clio-sync: protocol.rs 100/100, client.rs 100/92.97, client_feed.rs 100/96.39, http.rs 100/99.15, server.rs 100/95.51, crypto.rs 100/94.74, apply.rs 100/97.29; clio-store: postgres_sync.rs 100/100, sqlite_sync.rs 100/100 (functions/lines %).

issues.title: Race Condition and Flaky Test Failure on Rapid Item Updates (audit_events.id Collision)
issues.why_it_matters: Sub-millisecond updates to the same memory item crash with an internal SQLite UNIQUE constraint violation, causing intermittent test failures and runtime crashes.
issues.impact: Causes random test flakiness during sync apply and crashes in high-throughput or batch sync scenarios.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:37-38 uses now_iso() milliseconds for audit_id = format!("audit-upd-{}-{}", item.id, ts). Running cargo llvm-cov panicked: apply::apply_tests::t24_03_equal_stamp_tie_broken_by_score_then_device panicked at crates/clio-sync/src/apply_tests.rs:162:33: apply succeeds: AmError { code: Internal, message: "audit update: UNIQUE constraint failed: audit_events.id" }.
issues.proposed_fix: Append an atomic sequence number, microsecond/nanosecond component, or UUID suffix to audit_id in item_update.rs to guarantee uniqueness within the same millisecond.
issues.resolution: `update_audit_id` in crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs appends a process-wide atomic sequence to the millisecond stamp, so two updates of the same item in one millisecond cannot collide on audit_events.id.
issues.resolution_evidence: New regression coverage `suite_rapid_updates_unique_audit` runs 25 back-to-back updates on SQLite and Postgres (`sqlite_memory_item_suite`, `postgres_memory_item_suite`); make check 1185 passed / 0 failed.

issues.title: Client Push Change Feed Silently Omits Triples
issues.why_it_matters: Triples created or closed locally are never discovered by push_bank and never pushed to remote peers.
issues.impact: Multi-host deployments fail to sync facts/triples, causing divergence across nodes despite claimed sync support.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-sync/src/client.rs:205-237 only queries cfg.sync.feed_items() and cfg.sync.feed_assoc(). Although SyncStore::feed_triples is implemented in clio-store, push_bank never calls it. crates/clio-sync/src/client.rs:153-160 also omits feed_triples in pending_push calculation.
issues.proposed_fix: Call cfg.sync.feed_triples() in push_bank, convert closed triples into SyncMutation envelopes, and include them in the outbound payload; include triple feed count in sync_status pending_push.
issues.resolution: `client_feed::push_bank` now iterates `SyncStore::feed_triples`, packages each closed triple as a `triple`/`invalidate` mutation with SPO content, and `sync_status.pending_push` counts the triple feed. `client.rs` was split (<450 lines) to make room.
issues.resolution_evidence: End-to-end test `client_feed::client_feed_tests::triple_close_packages_as_invalidate_and_replicates`: A closes a triple, pushes, the relay journals the invalidate, and B's matching triple closes. `triple_packaging_skips_open_and_missing_triples` covers open/missing skip paths.

issues.title: Pull Loop Permanently Stuck on Unopenable or Corrupted Ciphertext (Bypassing DLQ Quarantine)
issues.why_it_matters: If a client cannot decrypt an encrypted payload (wrong key, bad ciphertext, or tampering), pull fails with an unhandled error instead of quarantining the mutation to dead-letter.
issues.impact: The pull pipeline is permanently wedged. Because the mutation is never written to sync_dead_letter, the operator cannot call ack_skip to unfreeze the pull cursor.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-sync/src/client.rs:368 calls let bytes = key.open(cipher)?; in decrypt_for_apply. Any decryption error bubbles up through ?, terminating pull_bank without recording a dead-letter row.
issues.proposed_fix: Catch key.open() errors in decrypt_for_apply, quarantine the mutation into sync_dead_letter using quarantine(), and return Ok(None) so the pull cursor safely freezes and can be ack-skipped.
issues.resolution: `decrypt_for_apply` now quarantines an unopenable (wrong key / tampered) or non-JSON payload as `malformed` and returns `Ok(None)`, so the pull loop returns with a frozen cursor and a dead-letter row that `ack_skip` can clear, instead of propagating `?` and wedging the pull with no DLQ row.
issues.resolution_evidence: Test `client::client_status_tests::wrong_cipher_key_quarantines_then_ack_skip_unfreezes`: wrong key -> dead_letter_open 1, pull_cursor frozen, item absent; after ack_skip -> open 0, cursor advances, item still absent.

issues.title: Server Pull Fails with HTTP 500 on Mutations with Null or Empty content_sealed
issues.why_it_matters: If any journal row has NULL content_sealed, the server fails during pull serialization and returns HTTP 500.
issues.impact: Any sync client attempting to pull a page containing such a row receives an HTTP 500 error, halting replication.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-sync/src/server.rs:338-344: let sealed = row.content_sealed.clone().unwrap_or_default(); followed by serde_json::from_str::<clio_store::CiphertextEnvelope>(&sealed). If content_sealed is None, deserializing an empty string fails with EOF.
issues.proposed_fix: In journal_row_to_mutation, handle None / empty content_sealed gracefully by supplying an empty default JSON value rather than attempting to deserialize an empty string as a CiphertextEnvelope.
issues.resolution: `server::journal_row_to_mutation` serves empty plain content (`{}`) for a row with no sealed content (KMS-less writer) instead of deserializing an empty string into `CiphertextEnvelope`.
issues.resolution_evidence: Test `server::server_tests::pull_survives_unsealed_journal_row_without_http_500`: a NULL content_sealed row pulls with HTTP 200 and `{mode:plain,data:{}}`. Additional error-seam tests cover corrupt cipher rows and corrupt sealed envelopes.

issues.title: Asymmetric LWW Tie-Breaking Due to Missing Local Device ID on Stored Items
issues.why_it_matters: The LWW tie-breaker compares device IDs lexicographically when timestamps and scores tie, but the local device ID is hardcoded to "".
issues.impact: Remote mutations always win ties against local items regardless of lexicographical device ID ordering.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-sync/src/apply.rs:395 passes "" as existing device ID in lww_compare. Any non-empty incoming device_id will win ties.
issues.proposed_fix: Persist originating device ID in items or pass the local node device ID to allow true symmetric tie-breaking.
issues.resolution: `apply::lww_loser` now passes this node's device id (`engine.device_id`) as the existing side of `lww_compare` instead of the empty string, removing the 'any non-empty remote device wins a full tie' asymmetry. Full origin-device persistence is not added; it is recorded as a Known Limitation with a named debt owner.
issues.resolution_evidence: `t24_03_equal_stamp_tie_broken_by_score_then_device` now asserts a higher device id (`peer-z` > local `node-1`) wins a full tie; make check clean.

strengths: Comprehensive state machine and property test suite structure (P-no-readmit-divergence, P-dlq-blocks, P-cursor-crash).
Clean separation of crypto and storage: server-blind ciphertext storage prevents DEK leakage to the sync server.
Strict conformance to the 450-line file limit across all 45 staged files.
Well-architected MCP tool bindings (sync_serve, sync_push, sync_pull, sync_status, sync_ack_skip) with robust token masking.
regrets: The developer skipped running the full make check before staging, missing an obvious unused import compiler error.
The developer rationalized away the function coverage deficit instead of implementing tests for unhit functions or pruning dead code.
process_changes: Enforce running make check (which includes clippy -D warnings) as an automated mandatory pre-stage hook.
Disallow speculative dual codegen rationalizations when per-file function coverage is below 90%.
